presets.title: Build a gamepad-ready main menu
presets.summary: Create a centred title menu with Play, Options and Quit, wrap-around gamepad navigation and a 0.3 s intro, then validate and picture it.
presets.prompt:
Build the main menu `{{content_folder}}/UI/{{menu_name}}` for {{project}}.
1. If hyper_ui_validate is not available, the UI pack is off: say so and stop. hyper_memory_recall `UI palette fonts` and reuse what it finds. If it exists, hyper_ui_inspect it and stop unless its widget tree is empty; else create it with Epic's UMGToolSet CreateWidgetBlueprint (parent /Script/UMG.UserWidget). Keep its editor tab closed during plans.
2. One hyper_ui_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId) with widget.add, widget.set_property, widget.set_style, widget.set_slot and widget.set_navigation: CanvasPanel `Root`; VerticalBox `Menu` with anchors center, alignment 0.5,0.5 and auto_size true; TextBlock `Title` "{{game_title}}", font_size 48, color_and_opacity {{accent}}, bottom padding 24; Buttons `PlayButton`, `OptionsButton` and `QuitButton`, each h_align fill, padding 0,8, with accessible_text and a 24 pt TextBlock label; explicit up and down links between them and wrap at both ends. In the same plan, animation.create `Intro` (0.3 s), animation.add_float_track on Menu RenderOpacity `0=0, 0.3=1` and an eased animation.add_transform_track on Menu translation_y `0=30, 0.3=0`. Follow any reply still queued, running or awaiting_user_approval with hyper_operation_wait (bWaitThroughApproval true).
3. hyper_ui_validate it. Picture it: Epic's EditorAppToolset OpenEditorForAsset, then SlateInspectorToolset Screenshot.
4. If no palette was recalled, hyper_memory_remember the colours and font sizes as the project's UI style.
Report a PASS/FAIL table: 3 labelled buttons with accessible text, navigation wraps both ways, Intro 0.3 s with 2 tracks, validate 0 errors and 0 warnings. Show the screenshot on its own line.

placeholders.name: player_bp
placeholders.label: Blueprint that shows the HUD

presets.prompt:

1. If hyper_ui_validate is not available, the UI pack is off: say so and stop. If it exists, hyper_ui_inspect it and stop unless its widget tree is empty; else create it with Epic's UMGToolSet CreateWidgetBlueprint (parent /Script/UMG.UserWidget). Keep its editor tab closed during plans.
2. One hyper_ui_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId) with widget.add, widget.set_property, widget.set_style and widget.set_slot on a CanvasPanel root, positions keeping a 5% safe zone at 1920 x 1080:
- ProgressBars `HealthBar` (size 360,20) and `StaminaBar` (size 360,12): anchors bottom_left, alignment 0,1, positions 96,-84 and 96,-60, percent 1, fill_color_and_opacity #D94040 and #40C070;
- TextBlock `AmmoText` "30 / 90", font_size 32, justification right: anchors bottom_right, alignment 1,1, position -96,-54, auto_size true;

placeholders.name: target_score
placeholders.label: Target score
placeholders.hint: 0 to 100; about 85 for an aligned match.

placeholders.name: player_bp
placeholders.label: Blueprint that shows it for the test
placeholders.default: the player character Blueprint the game mode spawns

presets.prompt:
Rebuild the UI mockup {{mock_path}} as `{{content_folder}}/UI/{{widget_name}}` and score it until it matches.
1. If hyper_ui_validate or hyper_image_compare is not available, say which pack is off (UI or lighting) and stop. Open the mockup and note its pixel size and look.
2. If it exists, hyper_ui_inspect it and stop unless its widget tree is empty; else create it with Epic's UMGToolSet CreateWidgetBlueprint (parent /Script/UMG.UserWidget). Keep its editor tab closed during plans. Build it with hyper_ui_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId) using widget.add, widget.set_property, widget.set_style and widget.set_slot, at most 64 ops per plan. Follow any reply still queued, running or awaiting_user_approval with hyper_operation_wait (bWaitThroughApproval true). hyper_ui_validate: 0 errors.
3. With the unreal-blueprint skill, add it to the viewport on BeginPlay of {{player_bp}} as a test hook; hyper_blueprint_compile_validate it (revision from hyper_blueprint_snapshot; preview, then compile with its planHash and an operationId; hyper_operation_wait).

6. Remove the hook unless I asked to keep it, and recompile.
Report the rounds (change, score), then a PASS/FAIL table: final score at least {{target_score}}, validate 0 errors, hook removed; and what still differs. Show the mockup and final capture on their own lines.

presets.title: Wire a menu's buttons and click-test them in play
presets.summary: Bind each button of the selected menu to its action, focus the first button on open, then click every button with the playtest bot.

placeholders.name: actions
placeholders.label: What each button does
placeholders.default: PlayButton opens the level L_Start, OptionsButton shows the widget OptionsPanel, QuitButton quits the game
placeholders.hint: One action per button, by button name.

presets.prompt:
Wire the buttons of the menu {{selected_asset}} and click-test them in play.
1. If hyper_ui_validate is not available, the UI pack is off: say so and stop. Load it with Epic's AssetTools load_asset; hyper_ui_inspect it: list its Buttons, animations and panels.
2. With the unreal-blueprint skill: Epic's UMGToolSet BindToEventProperty OnClicked for each button, then in its event graph: {{actions}}. On Construct, play its first animation if it has one and SetKeyboardFocus on the first button. Show the menu on BeginPlay of {{owner_bp}} with the cursor visible and input mode UI only. Change nothing else.
3. hyper_blueprint_compile_validate both Blueprints (revision from hyper_blueprint_snapshot; preview, then compile with its planHash and an operationId; hyper_operation_wait): 0 errors. hyper_ui_validate the menu: 0 errors.
4. hyper_playtest_run with Bot steps: UiAssert on the menu's first text widget, Capture `menu`; for each button that keeps the menu open, UiClick it, then UiAssert on what it shows and Capture; click the level-changing button last and Capture. Never click one that quits, which ends the session: its row is INFO, resting on its bound event. hyper_operation_wait, then hyper_playtest_status.
Report a PASS/FAIL table with one row per button (event bound, action, click evidence), plus compile and validate rows. Show each capture on its own line.

presets.title: Find and replace placeholder text in your UI
presets.summary: Sweep a folder's Widget Blueprints for leftover 'Text Block', lorem ipsum and TODO strings, fix the ones it can infer and list the rest.

placeholders.name: patterns
placeholders.label: Placeholder patterns
placeholders.default: Text Block, New Text, Lorem ipsum, TODO, TBD, Placeholder

presets.prompt:
Find and fix leftover placeholder text in the Widget Blueprints under {{content_folder}}.
1. If hyper_ui_validate is not available, the UI pack is off: say so and stop. Epic's UMGToolSet ListWidgetBlueprints for the folder; load each with AssetTools load_asset and keep their editor tabs closed.
2. hyper_ui_inspect them with bIncludeTree true, up to 32 per call, following nextCursor. Flag text, hint text and tool tips that read like a placeholder ({{patterns}}) and visible labels that are empty.
3. Propose the real string for each from the widget's name and screen (a `QuitLabel` says "Quit"); ask me before writing any you cannot infer. Then one hyper_ui_apply_plan per Widget Blueprint (bDryRun false, fresh operationId) of widget.set_property text, hint_text or tool_tip ops only. Follow any reply still queued, running or awaiting_user_approval with hyper_operation_wait (bWaitThroughApproval true).
4. hyper_ui_inspect again and hyper_ui_validate each changed asset.
Report a PASS/FAIL table with one row per Widget Blueprint (placeholders found, fixed, left for me and why) and validate 0 errors; then the full list of old and new strings.

presets.title: Polish a screen against its mock-up
presets.summary: Render a Widget Blueprint at full size, score it against a mock-up with a heat map, fix the worst differences and render again until it matches.

placeholders.name: mockup
placeholders.label: Mock-up image in the project
placeholders.hint: A PNG or JPG inside the project folder.

presets.prompt:
Make `{{content_folder}}/UI/{{widget}}` match the mock-up `{{mockup}}` for {{project}}.
1. hyper_ui_render_review with targetPath the Widget Blueprint's object path, resolutions ["1920x1080"], referenceImagePath {{mockup}}, targetScore {{target}}, a sessionId named after the widget and note "start". If the lighting_lookdev pack is off, reference.diagnostic says so: review the layout without a score. Open the render and the heat map.
2. Name the three biggest differences from reference.worstRegions and the heat map, and the review's errors. hyper_ui_inspect the widget for the names and values to change.
3. Fix the worst one with one hyper_ui_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId); follow a reply still running or awaiting_user_approval with hyper_operation_wait (bWaitThroughApproval true).
4. hyper_ui_render_review again in the same session with a note naming the change. Repeat steps 2-4 until the score reaches {{target}}, it stops rising for three passes, or six passes are done.
Report each pass: the change, the score and its rise, the issues left. End with the final render and heat map paths on their own lines.

presets.title: Review a screen at 720p, 1080p and 1440p
presets.summary: Render a Widget Blueprint at three screen sizes at the project's UI scale and list clipped or tiny text, contrast, safe-zone, overlap and focus problems.

placeholders.name: backdrop
placeholders.label: Colour behind the UI (r,g,b 0-1)
placeholders.hint: Near the game view behind this UI, for the contrast check.

presets.prompt:
Review `{{content_folder}}/UI/{{widget}}` the way players will see it. Change nothing.
1. hyper_ui_render_review with targetPath the Widget Blueprint's object path, resolutions ["1280x720", "1920x1080", "2560x1440"] and backdrop {{backdrop}} (r, g, b, a 1). If the UI pack is off, say so and stop.
2. Open each PNG. A table per resolution: its UI scale, then every error and warning with the widget, its rect and the fix the message gives.
3. Group what repeats across sizes (a layout problem) apart from what only 720p shows (scale and room).
Report PASS when there are no errors at any size, else FAIL with the three fixes that matter most. Put the three PNG paths on their own lines.

presets.title: Review the HUD as it plays
presets.summary: Render the HUD instance on screen in Play In Editor, with its live values, and check its text, contrast, safe zone and focus.
presets.prompt:
Check `{{content_folder}}/UI/{{hud}}` while {{level}} plays, with its live values.
1. If Play In Editor is not running, start it with hyper_playtest_run and a short Wait step, and keep it running.
2. hyper_ui_render_review with targetPath the HUD's object path, bFromPlay true and resolutions ["1920x1080", "1280x720"]. If it answers not_found, the HUD is not on screen: say what shows it and stop.
3. Open the PNGs. List the errors and warnings with widget, rect and fix; note text that only overflows with live values (long names, big numbers).
Report PASS or FAIL per resolution, then the PNG paths on their own lines.
